gates.name: Added public C# types and members carry a doc comment
gates.checks: It reads the lines that the change adds to `.cs` files and names each public or protected declaration with no `///` line above it. It skips tests, generated files and overrides. Exit 2 means the change could not be worked out, and it never exits 3.
gates.fix: Add a `/// <summary>` doc comment above the declaration that the finding names.

gates.name: Test classes and methods that the change adds carry a Story trait with a real key
gates.checks: It reads only the lines that the change adds, in the test files under `paths.testRoot`. It fails on a test class or method that the change adds with no Story trait, and on a malformed key on an added line. LEGACY-0 stays allowed on older code, but never covers code that the change adds. Exit 2 means `paths.testRoot` is not set or there is no merge base, and it never exits 3.
gates.fix: Add a Story trait with the story key, such as `#42`, to the test class, or correct the malformed key.

gates.name: Test methods that the change adds or edits keep the Arrange, Act and Assert markers in order
gates.checks: It reads the xUnit `[Fact]` and `[Theory]` methods that the change touches, and needs each marker once, in the order Arrange, Act, Assert. A merged marker such as `// Act & Assert` counts as both, and an edited older method fails only on what the added lines break. Exit 2 means the change could not be read, and exit 3 means no test method changed.
gates.fix: Add the missing marker, put the markers in the order Arrange, Act, Assert, or split a test that acts and asserts twice.

gates.name: JSON wire names in C# and in specs are PascalCase
gates.checks: It scans the `JsonPropertyName` attributes under the source root and the property names in the specs, and fails on a snake_case or camelCase name. It skips external contract paths and system fields. Exit 2 means `paths.sourceRoot` is not set or the specs could not be parsed, and it never exits 3.
gates.fix: Rename the wire name to PascalCase, or remove the attribute when it only repeats the property name.

gates.name: A project reference that the change adds is used in the code of the project
gates.checks: It reads each `ProjectReference` that the change adds, and looks for a namespace of the target in the code of the referencing project. It reads text, so it misses a type that code finds at run time, and it skips analyzer references. Exit 2 means the change or a project file could not be read, and exit 3 means there is no added reference.
gates.fix: Remove the project reference, or keep it when code finds its types at run time and say so in the pull request.

gates.name: A project reference that the change adds points to a lower layer of `dotnet.layers`
gates.checks: It reads each `ProjectReference` that the change adds, and names a reference that does not point to a lower layer of `dotnet.layers`. A project in no layer, or in two, is named and not judged. Exit 2 means the setting has the wrong shape or the change could not be read, and exit 3 means nothing to check.
gates.fix: Point the reference at a project in a lower layer or remove it, or change `dotnet.layers` in `aisdlc.json` when the order itself is wrong.

gates.name: C# code uses the shared options, HTTP client, credential and base exception, not its own copy
gates.checks: It reads the `.cs` files under `paths.sourceRoot`. It warns about `IConfiguration` in a constructor, `new HttpClient()`, an own Azure credential, or an exception without the base exception. It skips tests, generated files, `Program.cs`, `Startup.cs` and service registration methods, and lists new breaks first. Exit 2 means a setting is missing or wrong, or the change could not be read, and exit 3 means there is no C# file.
gates.fix: Use the shared part that the finding names: an options class, the HTTP client factory, the credential helper or the base exception.

gates.name: A change to an endpoint that has a spec also changes that spec
gates.checks: It reads only the routes and DTO types on the lines that the change adds or removes. It checks that the spec for the same resource changed too, and does nothing for an endpoint with no spec. Exit 2 means CHANGED_FILES is set but there is no merge base. Exit 3 means there is no spec or no changed file.
gates.fix: Update the spec under `specs/` for the changed endpoint, or confirm that the wire shape did not change.

gates.name: Docs match the code they cite
gates.checks: It judges only the lines that the change adds, changes or removes, and lists older drift as not blocking. It fails on a constant or service that the change adds and the page lacks, or on a cited name that the change removed. It also fails on a bad name on a page line that the change adds. Exit 2 means `paths.sourceRoot` is not set or there is no merge base, and it never exits 3.
gates.fix: Update the page to name the code as it is now, or remove the reference to a file or a name that is gone.

gates.name: Line coverage stays at the baseline, and a gain of a point is written to the baseline file
gates.checks: It reads the coverage file of the test run. It fails when line coverage drops below the baseline, or rises a point or more and the baseline file did not move. It does not check the 80% target on new code. Exit 2 means the coverage file is missing or the change could not be read, and it never exits 3.
gates.fix: Add tests to bring coverage back up, or set `lineCoveragePercent` in the baseline file to the figure that the gate prints.
